preanalytics.title: Result quality starts
preanalytics.description: About 70 % of laboratory errors arise in the preanalytical phase — between the moment blood is drawn and the moment the sample is loaded onto the analyser. Since 2016 Viena Medical has been working systematically on the quality of preanalytics in Belarus: from reviewing standard tenders to picking properly sterilised components.
preanalytics.pillarsTitle: What preanalytical quality is built on
preanalytics.pillarsHint: ISO · CLSI · WHO · MoH Order No. 1123
preanalytics.pillar_vacuum_text: Filling the tube within ±10 % of the declared volume per ISO 6710 is the only way to guarantee the correct reagent-to-blood ratio.
preanalytics.pillar_sterile_text: Sterilising after final packaging (ANSI/AAM/ISO 11137) is the only way to guarantee 100 % sterility — unlike sterilising before packaging.
preanalytics.pillar_cap_text: A screw cap with a blood-repellent membrane removes the aerosol risk during centrifugation and transport to centralised facilities.
preanalytics.pillar_components_text: Needle, holder and tube from a single manufacturer — required by Article 23 of MoH Order No. 1123 and the WHO phlebotomy guidelines.

hero.description: Viena Medical is a private company specialising, since 2016, in the preanalytical phase of laboratory diagnostics: blood-collection vacuum systems, reagents and safe consumables. We work with manufacturers directly, never silently swap them for «analogs», and systematically push for ISO 6710, ISO 11137 and Directive 98/79/EC to be applied in Belarus on substance, not on paper.

manifesto.title: We don’t exist in order to
manifesto.p1: Laboratories rarely know what alternatives exist to their usual supplier, and the supplier rarely has an interest in telling them. An entire industry has lived in that gap for decades — «closed» systems, standard tenders written for a single brand and preanalytical purchases at double the price.
manifesto.p2: We started in 2016 to do things differently. Not to win a single tender — but to slowly make preanalytics and laboratory diagnostics in Belarus more transparent, and the budget more efficient. It is slow, sometimes uncomfortable work: we argue with customers, we argue with the regulator, we lose deals. That is the fair price for being useful.
manifesto.p3: We openly write to the Ministry of Health, the antimonopoly authority, the State Control Committee and even to the State Security Committee — and we just as openly publish that work. Not because we enjoy conflict, but because no systemic change happens without an honest public conversation.
manifesto.quote: “The lab gets exactly what was specified — and we share responsibility for the result.”

preanalytics.title: Preanalytics — our focus
preanalytics.p1: The preanalytical phase is the path of a sample from the patient’s vein to the analyser’s probe. It is the most fragile part of the laboratory workflow: international evidence consistently puts about 70 % of all laboratory errors right here. We built the company around this topic.
preanalytics.p2: Our first public letter on preanalytics was a point-by-point review of Belmedtekhnika’s standard tender for vacuum systems (Outgoing No. 04/16, 27 May 2016). One year later — a letter to the Minister of Health on the concrete defects of the Chinese tubes that ended up in 90 % of Belarusian healthcare facilities (Outgoing No. 3, 15 February 2017). Those two letters set the approach the company has lived by ever since.
preanalytics.quote: “Even the most expensive blood-collection system costs about 1–3 % of the total assay. Saving on it is a way to put the entire result at risk.”
preanalytics.p3: That is why our reference set is the international standards: ISO 6710 for vacuum systems, ANSI/AAM/ISO 11137 for finishing gamma sterilisation, EU Directive 98/79/EC, the CLSI H01-A6 / H03-A6 / H04-A6 guidelines and the WHO phlebotomy guidance. Inside Belarus — Order No. 1123 of the Ministry of Health, which we treat as the minimum bar for the entire preanalytical phase.

iso6710.title: Dosed vacuum
iso6710.note: Filling the tube within ±10 % of the declared volume — the only way to keep the reagent-to-blood ratio correct.

iso11137.title: Finishing sterilisation
iso11137.note: Gamma rays after final packaging — the only guarantee of 100 % sterility for all components.

directive.title: EU IVD Directive
directive.note: The baseline quality standard for all medical devices for in-vitro diagnostics.

clsi.title: H01-A6 · H03-A6 · H04-A6
clsi.note: Compatible components from different manufacturers built to a common production standard.

who.title: Safe phlebotomy
who.note: Phlebotomy guidelines — screw caps, no aerosol effect, single-use needles.

moh1123.title: No. 1123 · 10.11.2015
moh1123.note: Belarus’s national requirements for the preanalytical phase — the baseline bar for healthcare facilities.

moh.title: 8 years of dialogue —
moh.p1: Since 2018 we have been sharing a systemic analysis of laboratory procurement with the Ministry of Health, the antimonopoly authority, the State Control Committee and the State Security Committee: where monopoly pricing forms, how «closed» systems exclude analogs, what could be done differently.
moh.p2: Some of our proposals have already made it into regulations — simplified registration of medical devices with FDA/CE clearance, exemption from on-site inspections, the first attempts to admit analogs. Some questions remain open — and we keep asking them. Not a single one of those letters is convenient for us as a company in the short term: every one of them widens the competition we ourselves participate in.

founder.name:
Maksim S.
Harbatsevich
founder.p1: Maksim founded Viena Medical in 2016. Before that — more than ten years in the field: service engineering, product lines, talking to customers from district laboratories to national reference centres. The principles the company lives by today grew out of that practice.
founder.p2: By the nature of the work he spends a lot of time inside the international laboratory community — that is the natural environment for anyone who wants to understand how laboratory diagnostics works beyond a single country.
founder.p3: These things are not the goal — they are a side effect of what Maksim is genuinely interested in: the preanalytical phase, new diagnostic formats, sane regulation. If the trade-off were fewer certificates and more time talking with heads of clinical labs, he would probably pick the second one.

meta.title: MedNAIS™ — digital SOP execution and preanalytics KPI analytics
meta.description: MedNAIS™ by Samplify FZCO: Hub for SOP management, Assistant for step-by-step guidance on Apple Watch and Wear OS, Monitor for time-per-step KPI analytics, Logger for biospecimen transport monitoring. Deployed and supported by VIENA MEDICAL in Belarus.

hero.description: We turn paper SOPs into step-by-step guidance on smart watches and phones, capture time per step automatically and build an evidence trail for audits. VIENA MEDICAL deploys the MedNAIS™ platform by Samplify FZCO in clinical labs, blood-collection sites and specimen-transport services in Belarus.

errors.n: per quarter in a typical unit

hero.disclaimer: Illustrative targets from pilots and internal benchmarks — actual results depend on scope, baseline and adoption.

overview.title: A platform for the people who run preanalytics and bedside procedures every day
overview.lead: MedNAIS™ closes the gap between paper SOP documentation and real bedside execution: a procedure is uploaded to the cloud and within minutes appears on the nurse’s Apple Watch, on a courier’s phone or on the treatment-room terminal.
overview.body: Unlike a classic LIS or QMS, MedNAIS™ does not teach the manual — it walks staff through the procedure in real time, times every stage, captures deviations and builds an auditor-grade trail with time-stamps. Managers get objective KPIs, not self-reports; a new hire delivers the same protocol from day one; the patient receives the same standard of care regardless of shift or site.
bullets: Digital SOPs — PDF, Word or a built-in step editor with timing; versioning and roles included.
Hands-free guidance on Apple Watch and Wear OS — voice, gesture, vibration; sterile mode without touching the screen.
Time-per-step analytics — bottleneck detection, objective comparison between operators, coaching without surveillance.
Transport monitoring — temperature, humidity, vibration, light, GPS and real-time alerts over LTE-M.

applications.title: Application areas for the Belarus and CIS market
applications.subtitle: MedNAIS™ is purpose-built for medical and laboratory practice. Six typical scenarios where the platform pays back the fastest.

items.title: Standardising preanalytics across dozens of sites
items.body: Single versioned SOPs for venous, arterial and capillary collection, a single quality scale and transparent per-site KPIs. Fewer rework cycles, fewer preanalytical errors in the final result.

items.title: Nurse onboarding in 2 days instead of 2 weeks
items.body: A new hire ships from their first shift: the watch guides them step by step, the supervisor sees timing and deviations in Monitor. Closes the staffing gap without sacrificing standardisation.

items.title: At-home specimen collection on the same SOP and trail
items.body: A mobile nurse visiting a patient with disabilities, an oncology patient or a non-ambulatory elderly client gets the same step-by-step instruction on their phone as the in-clinic team. Timing and geolocation are captured — for insurer contracts and audits.

items.title: CPAT and workshops on preanalytics (CLSI, ISO 15189, WHO)
items.body: Digital SOPs power the training modules: the student walks through the procedure step by step, the instructor sees timing and quality in Monitor. Samplify’s CPAT tool assesses current practice and produces actionable recommendations.

items.title: Cold-chain control and continuity of the transport corridor
items.body: A Logger in every thermal container or vehicle: temperature, humidity, vibration, light, GPS and case-opening — live. The alert reaches the team before the samples lose viability.

items.title: Audit-ready execution trail for clinical protocols
items.body: Every action and every step carries a time-stamp, an operator and a device. The full history can be reconstructed — for regulators, ISO 15189 accreditation, internal deviation reviews and validations.

rollout.title: How a rollout typically works
rollout.subtitle: Start with one unit and a small SOP set, then expand to watches, analytics and integrations. Mobile-first is the fastest path to ROI.

phases.label: Weeks 1–2
phases.title: Pilot and scope design
phases.body: Pick workflows, roles and devices (BYOD vs issued), formalise success metrics. Prepare the minimum SOP set and a pilot group.

phases.label: Weeks 3–6
phases.title: SOP digitisation and training
phases.body: Upload steps, validate the content with an expert, train super-users and frontline staff. Switch Assistant on for phones and, optionally, watches.

phases.label: Ongoing
phases.title: Measure, expand, integrate
phases.body: Review Monitor analytics with leadership. Add Apple Watch / Wear OS, Logger for logistics and extend SOP coverage to adjacent processes.

modes.name: Mobile-first
modes.body: The fastest path to value — phones only.

modes.name: Mixed
modes.body: Phones + watches by role and zone.

kpis.title: What changes in the numbers
kpis.subtitle: A benchmark from real deployments. Exact figures for your lab — sized during the pilot.

ethics.title: Analytics for coaching — not surveillance
ethics.body: Time-per-step and variance data are intended for process improvement, training and compliance evidence. Roles, access policies and a focus on workflow quality help teams adopt analytics without cultural pushback.

items.q: Which devices do we start with — do we have to buy watches?
items.a: No. Mobile-first is the most common pattern: step-by-step guidance works on iPhone (iOS 14+) and Android (8.0+). Apple Watch and Wear OS are added when the team needs hands-free or sterile workflows.
PDF, Word and a built-in step editor with timing. Versioning, roles and access are managed in Hub. Ready-made SOPs can be bought or sold on the SOP Marketplace.

The platform supports HIPAA-aligned practices: end-to-end encryption, role-based access control (RBAC), action logs. Storage and deployment options (including on-prem for regulatory needs) are scoped per customer.

items.q: How does Monitor connect SOPs and watches?
items.a: Every step a staff member executes in Assistant syncs to Hub and surfaces in Monitor: time, deviations, operator, device. That delivers KPIs for coaching and an audit trail for regulators.

items.q: What does Logger monitor during transport?
items.a: Temperature, humidity, vibration, illuminance, case-opening events and GPS — in real time over LTE-M via MQTT. Automatic alerts trigger as soon as a parameter falls outside the set range.

items.q: How do we get started in Belarus?
items.a: VIENA MEDICAL is the local partner of Samplify FZCO for MedNAIS™. We run a process assessment (CPAT), prepare a pilot, digitise the SOPs, train the team and provide ongoing support. Get in touch — we’ll schedule a demo.

cta.title: Let us show the platform on your own processes
cta.subtitle: We connect one treatment room or one mobile team to MedNAIS™ Hub in 1–2 weeks and measure the impact on your data. No payment before the contract is signed.
